📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid`
This is occurrence #154 (lifetime count; the 7-day count is distorted by the 11-19 gap catch-up).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (inert; see ownership.md)
Playbook: confirm the `Failed to Get Series Id for record -1` signature in ES, then compute errors/hits over the monitor's own 10m window. It's historically marginal, so don't over-escalate on the monitor alone. Diagnosis: `SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync` is called with recordId=-1 via `/v1/series/getseries` and doesn't guard against it (KB fix_status: proposed).
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 303750093 `[CRM][P1] ms-scheduler-api error rate high`, Warn 23:23:33Z -> Recovered 23:29:33Z. Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalink.

Root-cause analysis:
  • ES `fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND level.keyword:Error` 22:30Z-00:30Z returned 15 hits, all `Failed to Get Series Id for record -1 in table Activity` (the KB signature). APM errors ran at a steady 1-6 per 5m. That is the usual trickle, and a 10-min ratio crossed the 5% warn line.

Evidence:
  • Kibana (15 hits): https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-11-20T22:30:00Z',to:'2026-11-21T00:30:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service.keyword%3A%22ms-scheduler-api%22%20AND%20exceptions.Message.keyword%3A%22Failed%20to%20Get%20Series%20Id%20for%20record%20-1%20in%20table%20Activity%22'))
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.errors&exp_scope=service%3Ams-scheduler-api%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795213800&end=1795221000
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/303750093
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-21-b41d627ddf2d067b.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-02-tables-fields-fieldtablenameref-null-linked-fields`
This is occurrence #20 (lifetime count; the 7-day count is distorted by the 11-19 gap catch-up).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (inert)
Playbook: confirm `FieldTableNameRef Is Null` in ES, identify the tenant whose linked field has a null FieldTableNameRef, and repair the spider metadata. The write-path root cause is still unfixed.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 299251404 `Service tables-fields has a high error rate on env:prod`, Warn 23:45:24Z -> Recovered 23:50:24Z. Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalink.

Root-cause analysis:
  • ES `fields.dd_service.keyword:"tables-fields" AND level.keyword:Error` 23:35-23:55Z returned 80 logs, 54 with exception `FieldTableNameRef Is Null (Parameter 'FieldTableNameRef')`. The stack is `MetadataDataProvider.GetColumnForAllFields` (MetadataDataProvider.cs:1090) <- GetAllFieldsInstall <- FieldService.GetAllFields, via /v1/field/SaveViewBundleInternal. APM shows 3 errored requests at 23:45Z on `get_/v1/field/getfieldlistinternal` against about 178 hits per 5m, which tripped the 5-min 5% ratio.
  • Note: occurrence #20, so this also hits the every-10th resurface rule. The ES records carry no DB/account field, so the tenant can't be named from logs alone.

Evidence:
  • Kibana (54 hits): https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-11-20T23:35:00Z',to:'2026-11-20T23:55:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service.keyword%3A%22tables-fields%22%20AND%20level.keyword%3AError%20AND%20exceptions.Message.keyword%3A%22FieldTableNameRef%20Is%20Null%20%28Parameter%20%27FieldTableNameRef%27%29%22'))
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.errors&exp_scope=service%3Atables-fields%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795217400&end=1795219200
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299251404
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-21-4de54c694370ce6b.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #177 (lifetime count; the 7-day count is distorted by the 11-19 gap catch-up).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`sales management` usergroup / `#team-sales-management`, inert)
Playbook: confirm the dip is a brief drop below the fixed floor (not a data gap), confirm 0 `status:error` logs, and treat it as quiet-period noise.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302057011 `[CRM] runtime-core-subscriber throughput dropped (possible stall)`, 4 Triggered/Recovered flaps: 02:20:31Z, 02:46:31Z, 03:34:31Z, 03:40:31Z (each recovered in 1-11 min). Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalink.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:runtime-core-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()` 01:30-04:30Z: 180 points, 78 below the 2 msg/s floor (01:33-03:59Z), min 0.10/s @03:54Z, back to normal by 04:00Z. The 15-min profile is near-identical to 11-20 (02:15Z 0.03 vs 0.03; 03:45Z 0.21 vs 0.21). `service:runtime-core-subscriber status:error` returned 0 logs. This is overnight quiet-period noise against a fixed floor (4 flaps 02:20-03:41Z), not a consumer stall.
  • Sibling 302055141 (mobile-notifications-subscriber heartbeat, No Data 04:51Z, renotified hourly to 10:33Z) matched the same entry (occ #178). It was suppressed because this post reset the 24h window: a same-cycle ordering artifact (report ed020d1a).

Evidence:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aruntime-core-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795224600&end=1795235400
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302057011
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-21-3a03e02b6490a570.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`
This is occurrence #292 (lifetime count; the 7-day count is distorted by the 11-19 gap catch-up).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (inert)
Playbook: check p95 points over 3s and confirm latency-only (0 error logs). An isolated single-point spike is noise; a sustained run of points warrants an APM drill-down by screen id.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 115456700 `RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency`, Triggered 08:33:20Z -> Recovered 08:35:20Z. Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalink.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*}` 08:00-09:15Z: 135 points, exactly 1 over the 3.0s threshold (3.403s @08:33Z, ratio 0.13), back under on the next point. `service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod` 08:28-08:40Z returned 0 logs, so it's latency-only. An isolated spike at low weekend volume.

Evidence:
  • DD APM traces (>3s): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20resource_name%3Apost_%2Fapi%2Fv1%2Fruntime%2Fload%2F_screenid%2A%20%40duration%3A%3E3s&start=1795249500000&end=1795250700000
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Aruntime-core-api&exp_agg=avg&start=1795248000&end=1795252500
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/115456700
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-21-8a1aece2a8839e6c.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #51 (lifetime count; the 7-day count is distorted by the 11-19 gap catch-up).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (inert)
Playbook: re-query p95 over the monitor window and check 0 error logs; not user-impacting. *New this occurrence:* at 10s granularity it DOES reproduce, and only via SignalR long-lived transport spans (KB diagnosis updated). Suggest excluding `signalr/connect|reconnect|poll` from the monitor query.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302056327 `[CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high`, Triggered 09:31:07Z -> Recovered 09:41:07Z. Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalink.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} by {resource_name}` 09:15-09:45Z: the only over-threshold points are long-lived SignalR transports at 09:30Z (`get_/signalr/connect` 27,112s, `get_/signalr/reconnect` 18,915s, `post_/signalr/poll` 22.8s). Every short resource (health, send, ping, start, abort) stayed under 0.5s, hits were a normal 3-5k per 10m, and `service:notifications status:error` returned 0 logs. Connection-lifetime spans closing together, not request latency.
  • Gate note: the last notification was 11-20 09:43:07Z. That's 25.5h before this cycle's eval time (posted), but only 23.8h before this fire's ts (09:31:07Z). Disclosed per the cycle-eval-time anchor convention.

Evidence:
  • DD metric (p95 by resource): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request&exp_scope=service%3Anotifications%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795252500&end=1795254300
  • DD APM traces (signalr connect): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Anotifications%20resource_name%3Aget_%2Fsignalr%2Fconnect&start=1795252500000&end=1795254300000
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-21-ca1f87518168f519.md

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 4)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: env  •  alerts in group: 2
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `DevOps` (`devops` usergroup / `#team-devops`, inert)

Symptoms:
  - `[Valkey prod] Egress shaping: heavy hour` triggered twice on *production-redis-cluster-on-0001-002* (23:59:41Z and 00:21:41Z, recovered 01:31:41Z). 730,491 packets were shaped in the 00:00Z hour vs the 400k threshold (ratio 0.83).
  - Only node 0001-002 is affected. Nodes 0001-001 and 0001-003 show 0 allowance-exceeded in the same window (32 of 48 10-min buckets non-zero on -002, 20:00Z-02:40Z).
  - It is escalating. Over 30 days there were 441 non-zero hours on -002, but all 10 worst hours fall 11-18 to 11-21, and this is the first hour over threshold.
  - No client-side Redis command errors in APM (`trace.redis.command.errors` had no series 22:00Z-03:00Z), so there's no evidence of user-visible failure yet. Shaping adds latency first.

Trace IDs: n/a (infra metric)
Likely cause: read-heavy load skewed onto one replica (hot/large key or a scan-like reader), exceeding that node's per-instance egress allowance. The driving client is unidentified. Possibly related to the 11-20 mobile-notifications Redis hot path, but not confirmed: peak hours (19:00Z, 23:00-00:00Z) don't line up with the known SMS bursts.
Suggested next action: monitor. Have an operator with ElastiCache access check -002's client list / big-keys and the read-routing config before this trend crosses into errors. Upsizing the node type or rebalancing reads would clear it.

Source alerts (2 total): monitor 333494081, 23:59:41Z and 00:21:41Z. Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalink.

Score: +1 breach magnitude (0.83), +1 group size 2, +2 truly novel (no KB; only prior log line is the 10-16 creation artifact), 0 users (infra, unattributed), 0 critical-path.

Evidence:
  • DD metric (egress allowance exceeded, 0001-002): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=aws.elasticache.network_bandwidth_out_allowance_exceeded&exp_scope=cacheclusterid%3Aproduction-redis-cluster-on-0001-002&exp_agg=avg&start=1795197600&end=1795233600
  • DD metric (bytes out, 0001-002): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=aws.elasticache.network_bytes_out&exp_scope=cacheclusterid%3Aproduction-redis-cluster-on-0001-002&exp_agg=avg&start=1794614400&end=1795258800
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/333494081
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-21-f5ef6a9f985fa574.md
